title: Painting a Grid With Three Different Colors
summary: Given integers m and n, determine the number of ways to paint an m x n grid with red, green, or blue such that no two adjacent cells share the same color, modulo 10^9 + 7.
statement: Given integers m and n, determine the number of ways to paint an m x n grid with red, green, or blue such that no two adjacent cells share the same color, modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: Horizontally and vertically adjacent cells must have different colors.
hints: The narrow height makes an entire column a compact dynamic-programming state.
Enumerate vertically valid color columns and connect pairs that differ in every row.
Initialize one way per state; repeat n-1 times, summing compatible predecessor counts modulo the required modulus.
Every legal grid has one legal state per column and one compatibility transition between neighbors, so the DP counts every grid exactly once.

tests.explanation: A single cell can use any of the three colors.
Choose one of three colors, then either of the other two, giving six paintings.
